src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$There are many different aspects that affect the performance of simulations in$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$|Gromacs|. Most simulations require a lot of computational resources, therefore$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$it can be worthwhile to optimize the use of those resources. Several issues$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$|Gromacs| configuration$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* Don't use double precision unless you're absolute sure you need it.$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* Compile the FFTW library (yourself) with the correct flags on x86 (in most$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$  cases, the correct flags are automatically configured).$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* On x86, use gcc or icc as the compiler (not pgi or the Cray compiler).$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* On POWER, use gcc instead of IBM's xlc.$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* Use a new compiler version, especially for gcc (e.g. from version 5 to 6$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$  the performance of the compiled code improved a lot).$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* MPI library: OpenMPI usually has good performance and causes little trouble.$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* Make sure your compiler supports OpenMP (some versions of Clang don't).$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* If you have GPUs that support either CUDA or OpenCL, use them.$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$  * Configure with ``-DGMX_GPU=ON`` (add ``-DGMX_USE_OPENCL=ON`` for OpenCL).$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$  * For CUDA, use the newest CUDA availabe for your GPU to take advantage of the$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$    latest performance enhancements.$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$  * Use a recent GPU driver.$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$  * If compiling on a cluster head node, make sure that ``GMX_SIMD``$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$    is appropriate for the compute nodes.$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* For an approximately spherical solute, use a rhombic dodecahedron unit cell.$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* You can increase the time-step to 4 or 5 fs when using virtual interaction$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$  sites (``gmx pdb2gmx -vsite h``).$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* For massively parallel runs with PME, you might need to try different numbers$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$* For massively parallel runs (also ``gmx mdrun -multidir``), or with a slow$0

src/gromacs/gpu_utils/gpu_vec.cuh$  temperature and pressure coupling).$0
